entries.claim: Knowledge cannot write directly to the LITD Core; changes require decision, Guardian authorization, execution and evidence.
Governance state changes must be sequential, previewable, evidence-backed, idempotent and validated before registry writes.
contradictions: Multi-file JSON replacement cannot provide the same crash guarantees as a transactional database; rollback remains required.

entries.claim: Verified VEILLEUR V2 evidence must pass deterministic routing, confidence and counterevidence checks before becoming reviewable LITD Knowledge.
contradictions: A fixed confidence threshold is only a first calibration and may reject useful low-confidence signals.

entries.claim: EXPERIMENTAL LITD Knowledge may become ACTIVE only through an explicit, attributable human review that resolves contradictions and preserves a revalidation deadline.
contradictions: Human approval improves accountability but does not by itself prove that the underlying claim is true.

entries.claim: Only ACTIVE Knowledge may generate a review-only Core change candidate containing explicit impacts, risks, contradiction findings, tests and rollback.
contradictions: A declared affected-path list may remain incomplete until dependency analysis becomes repository-aware.
